verdict.rationale: SAM.gov's own Entity Management API lets a user look up an entity by UEI or legal business name and filter on registration status (samRegistered=No returns entities not registered/ID Assigned), so a founder could check their registration status. However, this requires a SAM.gov account and Public API Key, and the evidence shows no public web page for checking status. missing for 10: a documented public status-lookup page on sam.gov, keyless access, explicit registration/application status fields and stages, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, I can look up the status of my filing, application, or case from the service's public pages

citations.quote: samRegistered=No – to receive entities that are not registered/ID Assigned.
Unique Entity Identifier SAM Allows a single 12-character value or up to 100 values.
Users can make GET calls using any Browser or a Restful API client such as Postman.
registered users must obtain the API Key from the https://sam.gov/workspace/profile/account-details page using the field, “Public API Key”.
